analysis: Examined ClusterModelLayout.swift base and head plus the ClusterPlacementPlanner.swift patch excerpt. The changes are placement and memory-accounting logic. A new protocol hook, tensorParallelOverlapBytes, splits a divided tensor's loaded bytes into divided and replicated parts (head lines 392-397, 419, 461-476, 499-500, 525-538). The overlap helper rejects values outside 0...loaded (head 470-477), so per-rank byte counts cannot go negative or exceed the tensor. The default of 0 keeps the previous behaviour. The routed-expert divided total subtracts the overlap (head 529); it stays non-negative because overlap <= loaded. The planner change makes 'fastest' families ranked by speed comparison and prices an unmeasured link conservatively. The changes sit in the cluster placement library, which is outside the provider/coordinator WebSocket path, App Attest, key custody, prefix-cache storage and the add-on socket. They do not touch the listed assets (A-001 to A-019) or trust boundaries (TB-002, TB-007, TB-011, TB-012, TB-013). No auth, attestation, encryption, data-exposure or billing code is modified. Layout decode still caps input at 1 MiB and calls validate(). One residual question: ClusterModelLayout.validate() and tensorParallel?.validate(layout:) were not shown in full for the divided/replicated invariants. Replicated bytes can now rise on divided tensors, and the validator in another file may need to accept that. This is correctness and availability of placement, not a security issue. ClusterPlacementPlanner.swift was available only as a truncated patch excerpt, so its full logic was not reviewed. No concrete security regression identified.
